industry.key: P. Energy, commodities and metals mining
industry.why: Overweight, carried unchanged. Component 1 regime, 23-Oct-26 (risk-off confirmed and broadening: the discount-rate squeeze now a positioning wash-out in the artificial intelligence complex with credit leading it, bonds rallied as a hedge for the first time this cycle while the Fed still hikes in December, the US 10-year near 5.10%, Brent $111, French sovereign stress spilling into Italy, European defensives leading cyclicals on all five windows and breadth in the bottom fifth of three years; sources present 2026-W43): Brent $111 (Jefferies, 22 Oct), oil above $100 and rising, and energy led the week; energy is the hedge inside a European book against the shock that hurts everything else. Relative strength per 31-relative-strength.md, 2026-10-23 against 2026-08-21, not week on week: A now, A prior at industry level. Not Double Overweight at the industry because the industry holds Metals and mining (relative strength F now from A) and Agriculture beside the three energy sectors; Downstream distribution carries the A. Counter-case: Goldman attributes part of the oil move to restocking, two months into leadership is where reversals begin, and 13 of the 18 upstream Pool names read F on TSR/Valuation, so the market has paid.

sector.key: P.3. Energy - services and engineering contractors
sector.why: Overweight, carried unchanged. Component 1 regime, 23-Oct-26 (risk-off confirmed and broadening: the discount-rate squeeze now a positioning wash-out in the artificial intelligence complex with credit leading it, bonds rallied as a hedge for the first time this cycle while the Fed still hikes in December, the US 10-year near 5.10%, Brent $111, French sovereign stress spilling into Italy, European defensives leading cyclicals on all five windows and breadth in the bottom fifth of three years; sources present 2026-W43): Brent $111 keeps activity funded; oil services against integrated oil was not spoken to this week. Relative strength per 31-relative-strength.md, 2026-10-23 against 2026-08-21, not week on week: B now, C prior. Eight Pool names (SBM Offshore third on the starting score, Tenaris, Odfjell Drilling, Saipem, Subsea 7). One notch, not two, because this is the most operationally geared, smallest-company end of energy and the Fragility axis punishes that; back to C if Sell-side Momentum on the eight names falls further.

geography.why: Underweight, carried unchanged with the reason strengthened. Component 1 regime, 23-Oct-26 (risk-off confirmed and broadening: the discount-rate squeeze now a positioning wash-out in the artificial intelligence complex with credit leading it, bonds rallied as a hedge for the first time this cycle while the Fed still hikes in December, the US 10-year near 5.10%, Brent $111, French sovereign stress spilling into Italy, European defensives leading cyclicals on all five windows and breadth in the bottom fifth of three years; sources present 2026-W43): the spillover from France to Italy is the new fact this week (Goldman, 16 Oct, 'tentative spillover to Italy'), and the Italian listings in the Pool are bank-heavy (Monte dei Paschi, Credito Emiliano, Mediobanca) beside global businesses (Eni, Saipem, Tenaris, STMicroelectronics, Technoprobe, Reply). Not Double Underweight because Goldman also says contagion risk is lower than in 2011-15, its fragmentation index shows risk 'remains limited', and Southern European banks are healthier; relative strength is not graded by country. Moves to F if the fragmentation index rises or the Italian premium is read above 150 basis points; back to C under 100.
